signals.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant
signals.summary: Google Deepmind uses AI agents to run experiments on their own for upcoming Gemini models. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement.
signals.implication: Reassess role boundaries and human override for community deployments.
signals.long_summary: Google DeepMind is utilizing AI agents to autonomously conduct experiments for its forthcoming Gemini models. Despite this advancement, research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu indicates that the lab is still not close to achieving recursive self-improvement in AI systems. This progress in AI capabilities highlights the ongoing evolution of AI research and deployment, which is crucial for the community to understand as it navigates the implications and potential of AI technology.

signals.title: OpenAI wants companies to trust it with sensitive work by promising not to look at their data
signals.summary: OpenAI is testing a new feature called "Private Inference" that lets companies run queries on its most powerful models without OpenAI being able to access the data. The article OpenAI wants companies to trust it with sensitive work by promising not to look at their data appeared first on The Decoder .
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: OpenAI is currently testing a feature named "Private Inference," which allows companies to make queries using its advanced models while ensuring that OpenAI cannot access the data involved. This development aims to build trust among businesses by safeguarding their sensitive information during the AI interaction process. Understanding features like Private Inference is significant for our community as it highlights evolving standards in data privacy and security within AI, crucial for businesses considering AI adoption.
